newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: IVORIAN 97/98 MAIN COCOA CROP SEEN UP TO 1.1 MLN T. [CORRECTED 17:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: IVORIAN 97/98 MAIN COCOA CROP SEEN UP TO 1.1 MLN T. [CORRECTED 17:50 GMT]

text.p: Ivory Coast's 1997/98 (October-April) main crop is set to reach up to 1.1 million tonnes depending on the weather over the next four to five weeks, an industry crop analyst said on Tuesday.

"That is a figure based on what is on the trees, not from a trend," he said, adding that pod distribution showed that 45-50 percent of the main crop would arrive at ports in months up to the end of 1997, against a more usual 50-55 percent. The analyst declined to be identified.
"It is only slightly later than usual," he added, although harvesting would nevertheless begin in October.

He said the forecast, based on pod counts including developing fruits, showed a 1997/98 main crop similar or slightly above 1996/97 levels, which he put at 1.01 million tonnes by April 29, 1997 (corrects from 1996) -- the end of the main crop.
"The (1997/98) main crop will be similar or slightly higher," he said. "Whether that will be the case in four to five weeks remains to be seen as we have to be a bit more careful this year."

August pod counts were a good indication of following main crop sizes but rains into mid-September would ensure survival of pods already on trees into the new crop season. "The next month's rains are critical," he said. Weather after that would have less effect on harvests as all of the main crop would by then have developed.
